Question Paper  
Exam Date & Time: 30-Dec-2025 (09:30 AM - 12:30 PM)  
  
  
  MANIPAL ACADEMY OF HIGHER EDUCATION  
  MANIPAL INSTITUTE OF TECHNOLOGY - BENGALURU  
  THIRD SEMESTER B.TECH. DEGREE, MAKEUP EXAMINATIONS - DECEMBER 2025  
  Object Oriented Programming [ECM_2124]  
Marks: 50                                                                                                   Duration: 180 mins.  
  
  PART-A  
Answer all the questions.  
  
1)                Define encapsulation in Java and explain its importance.                                               (2)  
  
  
  A)                                                         Course Outcome: "CO1" / Cognitive Level: "Remember"  
  
  B)           Compare method overloading and method overriding with suitable examples.                               (3)  
  
  Course Outcome: "CO1" / Cognitive Level: "Remember"  
  
  C)           Write a Java program to define a class Employee with data members empId, name, and salary.             (5)  
  Include the following:  
  i) A parameterized constructor to initialize empId and name.  
  ii) A method setSalary() to assign salary.  
  iii) A method display() to display details.  
  In main(), create an array of employees, initialize them, and find the average salary of all  
  employees.  
  
  Course Outcome: "CO1" / Cognitive Level: "Create"  
  
2)                Write short notes on the following with one-line code snippets: (i) this (ii) super.                   (2)  
  
  
  A)                                                         Course Outcome: "CO2" / Cognitive Level: "Remember"  
  
  B)           Write a Java program to find the perimeter and area of a rectangle using parameterized                 (3)  
  constructors.  
  
  Course Outcome: "CO1" / Cognitive Level: "Application"  
  
  C)           Develop a Java program for an employee record system: Create a class Employee {String name;            (5)  
  int id; double salary;} with suitable constructors and a method display(). Create an array of five  
  employees, write their data to a file named employees.txt, read back, and display all records.  
  
  Course Outcome: "CO1" / Cognitive Level: "Application"  
  
3)                Mention differences between final and finally in Java with examples.                                   (2)  
  
  
  A)                                                        Course Outcome: "CO1" / Cognitive Level: "Understand"  
  
  B)           Explain the concept of abstract methods and abstract classes in Java with an example.                  (3)  
  
  Course Outcome: "CO2" / Cognitive Level: "Understand"  
  
  Page #1

C)                Write a Java program for user-defined exceptions that validate student marks. If internal marks       (5)  
  exceed 25, throw InternalMarkException; if external marks exceed 75, throw  
  ExternalMarkException. Display appropriate messages for each case.  
  
  Course Outcome: "CO2" / Cognitive Level: "Application"  
  
4)                        Write two differences between yield() and sleep() methods in multithreading.                          (2)  
  
  
  A)                                                              Course Outcome: "CO3" / Cognitive Level: "Analysis"  
  
  B)                Explain the concept of exception hierarchy in Java. Write a program to handle ArithmeticException     (3)  
  and ArrayIndexOutOfBoundsException.  
  
  Course Outcome: "CO3" / Cognitive Level: "Understand"  
  
  C)                Write a Java program that creates two threads: one to display even numbers and another to display (5)  
  odd numbers from 1 to 10 using synchronization to avoid interference.  
  
  Course Outcome: "CO3" / Cognitive Level: "Analysis"  
  
5)                        Explain the use of (? extends) in java generics with example.                                         (2)  
  
  
  A)                                                           Course Outcome: "CO4" / Cognitive Level: "Application"  
  
  B)                Write a generic method getMiddle() that takes an array of any type and returns its middle element.    (3)  
  Demonstrate with Integer and String arrays.  
  
  Course Outcome: "CO4" / Cognitive Level: "Application"  
  
  C)                Define a generic interface Transformer< T, R> with a method transform() that converts a value of      (5)  
  type T to R. Implement a class DoubleToStringTransformer that converts a Double to its formatted  
  String. Demonstrate usage with test cases.  
  
  Course Outcome: "CO4" / Cognitive Level: "Create"  
  
  
  -----End-----
